name: Patrice Harris
current_role: Former president of the American Medical Association; Hurun lists her as a founder of eMed (current eMed role not confirmed)
profile: Psychiatrist from Bluefield, West Virginia, with WVU degrees and Emory training. She ran Atlanta/Fulton County health services and in 2019 became the AMA's 174th president, the first African-American woman in the role. Hurun lists her as a founder of eMed, the at-home testing and GLP-1 digital health company valued at about $2B. eMed is now led by CEO Linda Yaccarino.
interesting_fact: She was elected the AMA's 174th president, the first African-American woman in the role, and chaired the AMA Opioid Task Force, launched in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: From 2001 to 2003, funded by the Arthur M. Blank Family Foundation, she was a senior policy fellow and lobbyist for Emory's Barton Child Law and Policy Clinic, working to protect children from abuse and neglect.
notes: Identity marked uncertain only because eMed's current site and her Wikipedia page do not mention her eMed role; the person (former AMA president) is unambiguous. She may no longer be at eMed (leadership now Yaccarino, Tom Brady, Dr. Dyan Hes), so the eMed press address may not reach her. Web search budget ran out before this could be verified. WVU also notes she was the first African-American woman to chair the AMA Board of Trustees (2016): https://eberly.wvu.edu/news-events/eberly-news/2016/06/20/patrice-harris-wvu-grad-and-bluefield-native-becomes-first-african-american-woman-to-lead-american-medical-association-board-of-trustees

name: Ashley Olsen
current_role: Co-founder and creative director (with twin Mary-Kate Olsen), The Row (New York)
profile: Former child actor (Full House, with twin Mary-Kate) who co-founded the luxury label The Row in New York in 2006. The brand won CFDA Womenswear Designer of the Year in 2012 and 2015 and Accessories Designer of the Year in 2014, 2018 and 2019. In 2024 the Wertheimers (Chanel's owners) and Françoise Bettencourt Meyers bought stakes valuing it at about $1B; the Olsens remain majority owners.
interesting_fact: The Row is named after London's Savile Row. For its first three years the Olsens kept their names off the brand and gave no interviews about it.
deep_cut_fact: The Row began in 2005 as Ashley's personal quest for the 'perfect T-shirt', which she tested on women of different ages and body types. The first collection had seven pieces, and Barneys New York bought all of them.
notes: Famously private: no public social media, and rarely gives interviews. No published press email found on therow.com. Best route is likely through The Row's PR or the press office of a fashion week, which needs a manual check.
